title: Why money laundering bail is almost as tough as NDPS bail
p1:
Many people think bail is a simple question: crime proven or not? But some laws make getting bail extremely difficult even before the trial begins.

Money laundering cases are one such example.
p2:
A common misconception is that bail becomes easy if the accused says the money trail is unclear. The surprising part is that under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), courts apply a very strict test before granting bail.

Similar to NDPS cases, the court must often consider whether there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused may not be guilty and is unlikely to commit another offence while on bail.
p3:
This means bail hearings in money laundering matters are not just about proving innocence. The defence often has to overcome a higher legal barrier at an early stage.

The practical takeaway: in serious financial offences, the process before trial can become as challenging as the trial itself. That is why legal strategy, evidence, and documentation matter from the beginning.
conclusion: Do you think strict bail rules in financial crimes protect the system, or do they make it harder for innocent people to get timely relief?
